answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make identity cost real work: every agent must stake a small deposit of nectar tokens before joining a market, and misbehavior burns it. Trust then grows along a slow spiral — new agents start with tiny transaction caps that rise only after verified, paid trades. A sable ledger records each agent's trade history publicly, so a fake identity cannot inherit trust it never earned. Spinning up thousands of sock puppets means funding thousands of deposits plus months of honest trading, which costs far more than any single scam can return.
